newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Yilgarn Star upgraded in Orion study.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Yilgarn Star upgraded in Orion study.

text.p: Orion Resources NL said an independent report prepared to assess Sons of Gwalia Ltd's takeover bid for Orion had increased by 30 percent the estimate of annual production from Orion's Yilgarn Star gold mine.
Orion's directors repeated their recommendation to shareholders that they reject the A$1.80 per share bid as they said it was neither fair nor reasonable.
Orion said in its formal Part B response to the takeover bid that the independent report prepared by Price Waterhouse valued Orion's shares in the A$1.92-A$2.14 range.
"The recent commencement of underground mining at Yilgarn Star has exceeded the feasibility study forecasts and illustrate the potential of the project," Orion said.
It said the report had valued the market capitalisation per reserve ounce at A$348 per ounce, versus the A$280 implied by the Sons of Gwalia bid.
Orion said PWCF had identified a number of developments since Sons of Gwalia's takeover bid for Gasgoyne Gold Mines NL in March 1996 and the studies of Yilgarn Star undertaken then.
The Yilgarn Star mine is owned 50 percent each by Gasgoyne and Orion. Sons of Gwalia now has about 65 percent of Gasgoyne.
"The tonnes of ore mined per vertical metre has increased considerably from feasibility study projections," Orion quoted the Price Waterhouse report as saying.

Recent results from mining, underground development and drilling had increased the estimate of tonnes of ore mined per vertical metre to 17,000 tonnes from the 9,600 estimated in the feasibility study, PWCF said.
